think.q: React warns "A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled". Usual cause?
opts: value started as undefined (e.g. user.name before load) and later became a string
why: Start with value="" (or value={x ?? ""}).

think.q: Which input should usually be uncontrolled?
opts: A search box that filters as you type
A price field that only accepts digits
A field whose value another field depends on
why: A file input's value can only be set by the user, so it is always uncontrolled.

try.task: Write PhoneInput({ onValid }): a controlled input that keeps only digits, max 10. When exactly 10 digits are entered, show "✓ valid" and call onValid(number) once per change.

takeaway.key: Controlled = state is the truth (validate/transform on each change). Uncontrolled = DOM is the truth (read via ref or FormData). Never switch between them.
mistakes: Expecting defaultValue changes to update the field.

try.task: Write validate(values) (pure: returns an errors object) and SignupForm({ onSubmit }): email must contain "@", password at least 8 chars. On submit show errors (role="alert"), else call onSubmit({ email, password }).
examples: validate({ email: "x", password: "123" })  // { email: "Enter a valid email", password: "At least 8 characters" }
try.hint: Controlled inputs with labels "Email" and "Password"; on submit: const errs = validate(values); setErrors(errs); if no keys, onSubmit(values).

tests.code:
import { render, screen, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react'
import { expect, test } from 'vitest'
import { SignupForm, validate } from './SignupForm'

test('validate returns errors for bad values', () => {
  expect(validate({ email: 'x', password: '123' })).toEqual({ email: 'Enter a valid email', password: 'At least 8 characters' })
  expect(validate({ email: 'a@b.c', password: '12345678' })).toEqual({})
})

test('shows errors and does not submit', () => {
  const got = []
  render(<SignupForm onSubmit={(v) => got.push(v)} />)
  fireEvent.click(screen.getByText('Sign up'))
  expect(screen.getAllByRole('alert')).toHaveLength(2)
  expect(got).toHaveLength(0)
})

test('submits valid values', () => {
  const got = []
  render(<SignupForm onSubmit={(v) => got.push(v)} />)
  fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText('Email'), { target: { value: 'a@b.c' } })
  fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText('Password'), { target: { value: '12345678' } })
  fireEvent.click(screen.getByText('Sign up'))
  expect(got).toEqual([{ email: 'a@b.c', password: '12345678' }])
  expect(screen.queryByRole('alert')).toBeNull()
})

checks.t: validate returns errors for bad values
shows errors and does not submit

takeaway.key: Form = state + a pure validate(values) + a submit handler with preventDefault. Tie errors to inputs with aria attributes.
mistakes: Buttons without type="button" submitting the form.

dryRun.title: URL /users/42/posts with routes users/:id → posts
dryRun.note: A router maps URL paths to components. Nested routes render inside their parent's <Outlet />; :id segments become params; <Link> changes the URL without a page reload (history.pushState). Data routers add loaders (fetch before render) and actions (form submits).

think.q: Why use <Link to="/about"> instead of <a href="/about"> inside the app?
opts: a tags are not allowed in React
Link changes the URL with the History API and re-renders, without a full page reload
why: A plain a would reload the page and lose all state.

think.q: Route path "products/:slug", URL /products/blue-shirt. How do you read "blue-shirt"?
why: useParams returns the dynamic segments of the matched route.

think.q: A parent route renders a layout but children never appear. What is missing?
why: The parent decides where its matched child renders.

think.q: After deploying a SPA, refreshing /users/42 gives 404 from the server. Fix?
opts: Serve index.html for unknown paths (SPA fallback) so the client router can handle the URL
why: The server has no file /users/42; the router only lives in the browser.

think.q: What does a route loader give you over fetching in useEffect?
opts: It runs only on the server
Data starts loading on navigation, before the component renders, with no loading waterfall inside effects
why: Effects fetch after render, then children fetch after their render: a waterfall.

try.task: Write matchPath(pattern, path): return an object of params when the path matches the pattern, else null. Segments starting with ":" capture; "*" at the end matches the rest (as params["*"]); trailing slashes are ignored.
try.hint: Split both on "/" (filter empties). Walk the pattern parts; decodeURIComponent captured values.

takeaway.key: Routes map paths to components; nested routes render in <Outlet/>; :params via useParams; Link navigates without reload; loaders fetch before render.
mistakes: Plain a tags for in-app links.

dryRun.title: Class lifecycle vs hooks
dryRun.note: New code uses function components and hooks. You still meet classes in older code, and error boundaries still need one. The mental shift: classes think in lifecycle moments; hooks think in synchronising with values.

think.q:
class A extends Component {
  constructor(p) { super(p); console.log('constructor') }
  componentDidMount() { console.log('didMount') }
  render() { console.log('render'); return null }
}
why: Construct, render, then mount after the DOM is updated.

think.q:
class C extends Component {
  state = { n: 0 }
  render() { return <button onClick={() => { this.setState({ n: this.state.n + 1 }); this.setState({ n: this.state.n + 1 }) }}>{this.state.n}</button> }
}
why: Same batching rule as hooks: both read the old state. Use the updater form setState((s) => …).

think.q:
class T extends Component {
  state = { v: 'x' }
  handle() { return this?.state?.v ?? 'lost this' }
  render() { const h = this.handle; return <p>{h()}</p> }
}
why: A class method called without its object loses this (class bodies are strict). Classes need bind or arrow fields; hooks avoid this entirely.

think.q: What still requires a class component in React 19?
why: Everything else has a hook.

think.q: How do you move componentDidUpdate(prevProps) logic comparing userId to hooks?
why: List the value in deps; React runs the effect when it changes.

takeaway.key: Use function components and hooks; know the class lifecycle to read old code; error boundaries still need a class.
mistakes: Thinking hooks map 1:1 to lifecycle methods.
